summary: Before Shabbos we may wrap a pot to keep it warm, but not in things that make it hotter. This mishnah lists what we may and may not wrap it in.
stIntro: When a pot is removed from the fire on Shabbat eve it may be insulated in materials that preserve its heat, but not in materials that increase its heat. Raising the temperature of a pot is tantamount to cooking. The mishnayot that follow list those materials in which such a pot may be insulated on Shabbat eve and those materials in which it may not be insulated.

chunks.en: In what may we wrap a pot, and in what may we not wrap it?
chunks.st: In what may one insulate a pot of cooked food on Shabbat eve, and in what may one not insulate it?

chunks.he: אֵין טוֹמְנִין לֹא בְגֶפֶת וְלֹא בְזֶבֶל,
chunks.en: We may not wrap it in olive pulp, or in manure,
chunks.st: One may neither insulate it in the solid residue of produce that has been pressed free of its oil, nor in manure,

chunks.he: לֹא בְמֶלַח וְלֹא בְסִיד וְלֹא בְחֹל,
chunks.en: or in salt, or in lime, or in sand,
chunks.st: nor in salt, nor in lime, nor in sand,

chunks.en: whether they are wet or dry.
chunks.explain: These things make heat by themselves.
chunks.st: whether those materials are moist or whether they are dry. All of these materials spontaneously generate heat when piled for an extended period. Therefore, they add heat to a pot insulated in them. And one may

chunks.he: לֹא בְתֶבֶן וְלֹא בְזָגִים וְלֹא בְמוֹכִים
chunks.en: Not in straw, grape skins, or soft rags,
chunks.st: neither insulate a pot in straw, nor in the residue of grapes that have been pressed for their juice, nor in soft material, e.g., from tattered clothing,

chunks.en: and not in grass, when they are wet,
chunks.st: nor in grass, when these materials are moist.

chunks.en: but we may wrap in them when they are dry.
chunks.st: However, one may insulate a pot in them when they are dry.

chunks.en: We may wrap a pot in clothing, or in produce,
chunks.st: One may insulate a pot of hot food on Shabbat eve in clothing, in produce,

chunks.en: in dove feathers, in a carpenter's sawdust,
chunks.st: in doves’ wings, in a carpenter’s wood-shavings,

chunks.en: and in thin flax fibers.
chunks.st: and in the chaff of fine flax.

chunks.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹסֵר בְּדַקָּה וּמַתִּיר בְּגַסָּה:
chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah forbids thin ones and allows thick ones.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda prohibits doing so when it is fine, and permits doing so when it is coarse.

summary: We may wrap a pot in animal skins or in wool, but wool is muktzeh, so we may not move it. The mishnah explains how to take out the pot, and teaches about covering a pot on Shabbos.

chunks.en: We may wrap a pot in animal skins,
chunks.st: One may insulate cooked food on Shabbat eve in animal hides

chunks.en: and we may move them.
chunks.st: and may move
chunks.stMore: those hides on Shabbat. So too, one may insulate food

chunks.en: In wool fleece,
chunks.st: in wool fleece and, in contrast to hides,

chunks.en: we may not move them.
chunks.st: one may not move the fleece.

chunks.en: So what does he do?
chunks.st: How, then, does one act
chunks.stMore: if he insulated food in fleece, and now wishes to remove the pot?

chunks.en: He lifts the cover, and they fall off.
chunks.st: He lifts the cover, which he is permitted to move, and the fleece falls by itself. He need not even touch it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says: If he placed the pot in

chunks.en: If it is in a basket, he tips it on its side and takes the pot,
chunks.st: a basket filled with fleece, he leans the basket on its side so that the fleece will fall to the side and takes the pot. Otherwise, there is concern

chunks.en: in case he takes it and cannot put it back.
chunks.st: lest the wool collapse when he lifts the pot from the basket. And then, he will be unable to replace
chunks.stMore: the pot, as it is prohibited to move the wool to make room for the pot, since the wool is set-aside.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis disagree and say:

chunks.en: he takes it and puts it back.
chunks.st: He may take the pot and afterward replace it. If

chunks.en: If he did not cover the pot while it was still day,
chunks.st: one did not cover a pot of cooked food on Shabbat eve while it was still day,

chunks.en: he may not cover it after dark.
chunks.st: he may not cover it after dark. However, if

chunks.en: If he covered it and it became uncovered,
chunks.st: one covered it while it was still day and it was uncovered on Shabbat,

chunks.en: he is allowed to cover it.
chunks.st: he is permitted to cover it even on Shabbat.

chunks.he: מְמַלֵּא אֶת הַקִּיתוֹן וְנוֹתֵן לְתַחַת הַכַּר,
chunks.en: One may fill a jug and put it under a pillow
chunks.st: One may fill a jug with cold water on Shabbat and place it beneath a pillow

chunks.en: or under a cushion.
chunks.st: or a cushion to prevent it from getting warm.
